correctness.rationale: For each fixed d≥2, stationarity yields independent Exp gaps for typical cell and independent Gamma(2) widths for zero cell, with zero-cell split fractions independent uniform. With X_i=λ_iW_i∼Gamma(k,1), T_i=−log X_i has density e^(−kt)h(t)/Γ(k), h=e^(−e^(−t)); decomposing h=H+q with ∫q=−γ and finite moments gives h^{*d}(s)=s^{d−1}/(d−1)!−dγ s^{d−2}/(d−2)!+o(s^{d−2}). Integration of e^(−ks) from L proves the two-term tail. The exact conditional joint density for (T_1/L,...,T_(d−1)/L,Z=S−L) converges pointwise a.e. to Dirichlet-simplex chart × Exp(k); both densities have total mass one, so Scheffé proves TV. Full d-vector convergence is only weak because finite-L hyperplanes and limiting simplex are singular. Independent Bessel lower-tail calculations d=2 for k=1,2 corroborate the constants, not the d-general proof.
